It is about an affair between an attractive thirty-two-year-old woman and a youth just short of legal majority.  Interlaced with explicit scenes of love making, the movie watches the two lovers trying to come to grips with their mutual attraction, sexuality and societal disapproval.

Kang Hye-jung stars in the lead role as a 20-year-old woman with the mental and emotional skills of a seven-year-old, who falls in love with a policeman she sees as her Prince Charming, but must face tragedy when she is forced to deal with certain realities about herself and those around her.
An Affair | An Affair () is a 1998 South Korean film.  The quiet film about a woman who falls in love with her sister's fiancé was the seventh-highest-grossing Korean film of 1998 and won the Best Asian Film award at the 1999 Newport Beach International Film Festival.
Happy End (1999 film) | Happy End is a South Korean film released in 1999.  Written and directed by Jung Ji-woo, it's about a woman who's having an affair while her husband is unemployed.

It premiered at the 2012 Sundance Film Festival and has received generally positive reviews from critics.
Just, Melvin: Just Evil | Just, Melvin: Just Evil is a 2000 American documentary by James Ronald Whitney about his grandfather, Melvin Just, and the devastating consequences of the sexual abuse Just inflicted on their family.  It premiered at the 2000 Sundance Film Festival and aired on HBO on April 22, 2001.  The film was well received overall; critic Roger Ebert called "Just, Melvin" "one of the most powerful documentaries I've seen."

Derek Cianfrance, Cami Delavigne, and Joey Curtis wrote the film, and Michelle Williams and Ryan Gosling played the lead roles as well as serving as co-executive producers for the film.  The band Grizzly Bear scored the film.
